nahw.text: Two categories of <bdi>حَرْف عَامِل</bdi>: {{c1::<bdi>حُرُوف الجَرّ</bdi>}}, which make the <bdi>اِسْم</bdi> they act on <bdi>مَجْرُور</bdi>; and {{c2::<bdi>الحُرُوف المُشَبَّهَة بِالفِعْل</bdi>}} (<bdi>إِنَّ</bdi> and her sisters), which put the <bdi>مُبْتَدَأ</bdi> into <bdi>نَصْب</bdi> and leave the <bdi>خَبَر</bdi> in <bdi>رَفْع</bdi>
nahw.extra: Both change the <bdi>إِعْرَاب</bdi> of the words after them — the mark of a <bdi>حَرْف عَامِل</bdi>.
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch. 1 — the ḥarf, §1.6 pronouns — class notes 2026-10-01

nahw.meaning: words that change the grammatical positioning of the <bdi>مُبْتَدَأ</bdi> and <bdi>خَبَر</bdi> — from <bdi>نَسْخ</bdi>, abrogation
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch. 1 — the ḥarf, §1.6 pronouns — class notes 2026-10-01

nahw.front: By their effect on the <bdi>مُبْتَدَأ</bdi> and <bdi>خَبَر</bdi>, to which class of words do <bdi>إِنَّ</bdi> and her sisters belong?
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch. 1 — the ḥarf, §1.6 pronouns — class notes 2026-10-01

nahw.front: Before what do <bdi>إِنَّ</bdi> and her sisters appear?
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch. 1 — the ḥarf, §1.6 pronouns — class notes 2026-10-01

nahw.text: <bdi>إِنَّ</bdi> and her sisters put the <bdi>مُبْتَدَأ</bdi> into {{c1::<bdi>نَصْب</bdi>}} and leave the <bdi>خَبَر</bdi> in {{c2::<bdi>رَفْع</bdi>}}
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch. 1 — the ḥarf, §1.6 pronouns — class notes 2026-10-01

nahw.front: Once <bdi>إِنَّ</bdi> enters a nominal sentence, what are its <bdi>مُبْتَدَأ</bdi> and <bdi>خَبَر</bdi> called?
nahw.back: <bdi>اِسْمُ إِنَّ</bdi> and <bdi>خَبَرُ إِنَّ</bdi> — named after the particle, so <bdi>اِسْمُ كَأَنَّ</bdi>, <bdi>خَبَرُ لَيْتَ</bdi> and so on
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch. 1 — the ḥarf, §1.6 pronouns — class notes 2026-10-01

nahw.front: Why are <bdi>إِنَّ</bdi> and her sisters sometimes called <bdi>الحُرُوف النَّاصِبَة</bdi>?
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch. 1 — the ḥarf, §1.6 pronouns — class notes 2026-10-01

nahw.text: A <bdi>حَرْف نَاصِب</bdi> such as <bdi>لَنْ</bdi> puts {{c1::a <bdi>مُضَارِع</bdi> verb}} into <bdi>نَصْب</bdi>; <bdi>إِنَّ</bdi> and her sisters, also called <bdi>الحُرُوف النَّاصِبَة</bdi>, put {{c2::the <bdi>مُبْتَدَأ</bdi> of a nominal sentence}} into it
nahw.extra: Same name, different targets — the ṣarf particle governs a verb, these govern a nominal sentence.
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch. 1 — the ḥarf, §1.6 pronouns — class notes 2026-10-01

nahw.extra: Six in all: <bdi>إِنَّ</bdi> and her five sisters — the whole list is to be memorised.
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch. 1 — the ḥarf, §1.6 pronouns — class notes 2026-10-01
